quotes.text: National Security Act, 1980: s.3(4) – Report to the State Government – Held: Once an order of detention is made, the officer making the order must forthwith report the fact to the State Government, together with the grounds on which the order has been made and other particulars which have a bearing on the matter.
Allowing the appeal, the Court HELD: 1. Right to make a representation: Constitutional safeguards and legislative scheme of the NSA

neutral_facts.value: The case involves an individual who was detained under the National Security Act, 1980. The detention order was initially passed on May 11, 2021, and the individual was detained on May 12, 2021. The order was approved by the State Government on May 13, 2021. The individual submitted a representation against the detention order on May 18, 2021, which was communicated to the State Government and Central Government on May 20, 2021. The Central Government received the representation on June 1, 2021, and the State Government received it on May 24, 2021. The Central Government rejected the representation on June 24, 2021, and the State Government rejected it on July 15, 2021. The individual was not informed of the rejection of the representation until it was communicated to him on June 28, 2021. The Supreme Court held that the delay in considering the representation and the failure to communicate the rejection of the representation violated the individual's constitutional rights under Article 22(5) of the Constitution. The order of detention was therefore invalidated.

quotes.text: The order of detention was passed on 11 May 2021 and the appellant was detained on 12 May 2021. The order of detention was approved by the State Government on 13 May 2021, upon which the State Government submitted the order of detention to the Central Government on the same day. On 18 May 2021, the detenu submitted a simultaneous representation before the District Magistrate, State Government and the Central Government.

key_evidence_accepted.value: The Supreme Court accepted the evidence that the State Government failed to communicate the rejection of the appellant's representation in a timely manner, and there was an unexplained delay in considering the representation.

quotes.text: The failure of the Central and State Governments to communicate the rejection of the appellant’s representation in a time-bound manner is sufficient to vitiate the order of detention.

defence_argument.value: The State Government was not bound to wait on the Advisory Board's report before deciding the representation and must do so as expeditiously as possible. The delay in communication was due to administrative procedures and did not violate the detenu's rights.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the constitutional principle that the communication of the grounds of detention and the opportunity to make a representation must be done as soon as may be, with immediacy, to ensure the detenu's right to a prompt and meaningful consideration of their representation.

quotes.text: The communication of the grounds of detention to the detenu 'as soon as may be' and the affording to the detenu of the earliest opportunity of making a representation against the order of detention to the appropriate government are intended to ensure that the representation of the detenu is considered by the appropriate government with a sense of immediacy.
